ai.literal: By easy approachability attaining is easy they say towards anyone possessing courtesy called proper conduct
ai.translation: The wise say that the proper conduct called courtesy towards everyone is easily attained by being easily approachable.
ai.modern: யாவரிடத்தும் எளிமையாகப் பழகும் தன்மையால், பண்புடைமை என்னும் நல்வழியை அடைவது எளிது என்று அறிஞர் கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the foundation of developing good character and courtesy. The key word 'eṇpatam' refers to being easily accessible and approachable to people without arrogance. By maintaining this openness and simplicity towards everyone, the noble path of courtesy is naturally and easily attained.

ai.literal: Possession of love, being born in a noble family, these two are the path called possession of good qualities.
ai.translation: Possessing affection and being born into a noble family—these two constitute the path known as true courtesy.
ai.modern: அன்பு உடையவராக இருப்பதும், சிறந்த குடியில் பிறந்திருப்பதும் ஆகிய இந்த இரண்டுமே பண்புடைமை என்று சொல்லப்படும் நல்வழியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the foundation of good character or courtesy. The first requirement is 'anpudaimai', which means possessing genuine love and affection for others. The second is 'aanra kudi pirathal', which means being born into a noble or excellent family, implying an upbringing rooted in good values. The word 'vazhakku' refers to the established path or proper nature of things. Together, these two traits form the path that is called true courtesy.

ai.literal: Physical feature resembling human resemblance is not indeed; highly worthy character resembling that which equals is resemblance.
ai.translation: Resembling others in physical form is not true human resemblance. Resembling them in excellent character is the only true resemblance.
ai.modern: உடலமைப்பால் மற்றவர்களைப் போல இருப்பது உண்மையான மனித ஒப்புமை ஆகாது. சிறந்த பண்புகளால் மற்றவர்களோடு ஒத்திருப்பதே உண்மையான ஒப்புமை ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines what makes someone truly human by contrasting physical appearance with inner character. The phrase "உறுப்பு ஒத்தல்" refers to having the same body parts as other people, which the poet states is not true human resemblance. Instead, true equality comes from "பண்பு ஒத்தல்"—sharing the excellent, worthy qualities ("வெறுத்தக்க பண்பு") that define humanity. The repetition of the word "ஒப்பு" (resemblance or equality) emphasizes that biological similarity is superficial, while moral character is the true measure of a person.

ai.literal: With amiability goodness practiced benefit possessors' character will praise world.
ai.translation: The world celebrates the character of those whose usefulness lies in practicing amiability and goodness.
ai.modern: நயமும் நன்மையும் பொருந்திய செயல்களைச் செய்யும் பயனுடையவர்களின் பண்பினை உலகம் பாராட்டும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet explains that true usefulness in life comes from combining amiability with moral goodness. The word 'nayan' signifies a pleasant, fair, and amiable disposition, while 'nanri' refers to righteous and good deeds. Those who possess the benefit of practicing these two traits are highly valued by society. Consequently, the world praises and celebrates their noble character.

ai.literal: Even in a joke, mockery is unpleasant; even in enmity, courtesy exists with those who know proper conduct.
ai.translation: Mockery is painful even when meant as a joke. But courtesy exists even during enmity among those who know proper conduct.
ai.modern: விளையாட்டிற்காகச் சொல்லப்படும்போதும் ஒருவரை இகழ்ந்து பேசுவது துன்பம் தருவதாகும். ஆனால், உலகத்தின் இயல்பை அறிந்தவர்களிடத்தில் பகைமையிலும் நல்ல பண்புகள் இருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts the pain caused by mockery with the grace of true courtesy. It states that belittling someone, even in jest, causes hurt. On the other hand, people who understand proper conduct maintain their good character and courtesy even towards their enemies. The juxtaposition highlights that true refinement never stoops to contempt, regardless of the situation.

ai.literal: Resting upon those who possess goodness, the world exists; if that is not so, having entered the earth, it will perish indeed.
ai.translation: The world endures because it rests upon people of noble character. If it did not, it would crumble into the dust and perish.
ai.modern: பண்புடைய மனிதர்களைப் பொருத்தே இவ்வுலகம் நிலைபெற்று இயங்குகிறது. அந்தப் பண்பு மட்டும் இல்லாவிட்டால், உலகம் மண்ணுக்குள் புதைந்து அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that the survival and functioning of the world depend entirely on people of noble character. The word 'பட்டு' indicates that the world's existence rests upon or is anchored by these good individuals. Without their sustaining virtue, the text vividly states that the world would simply sink into the dirt and cease to exist. The particle 'மன்' at the end adds a tone of absolute certainty to this inevitable ruin.

ai.literal: file resembling sharp ones even if, tree they resemble human quality those who do not have.
ai.translation: Even if their intellect is as sharp as a file, those who lack human decency are merely like trees.
ai.modern: அரத்தைப் போல கூர்மையான அறிவுடையவராக இருந்தாலும், மனிதர்களுக்கு உரிய நல்ல பண்பு இல்லாதவர்கள் மரத்திற்கு ஒப்பானவர்களே ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts intellectual sharpness with moral character. The word 'அரம்' refers to a file, a tool used to sharpen metal, symbolizing a highly honed and piercing intellect. However, the poet asserts that without 'மக்கட்பண்பு' (human decency or noble character), such intelligent people are no better than a 'மரம்' (a tree). A tree is alive but lacks human sensitivity and empathy, showing that mere intelligence without humane qualities renders a person emotionally and socially wooden.

ai.literal: Friendship not-doing having-become goodness without-things even-to-those-who-do, good-character not-doing becoming lowest.
ai.translation: It is the lowest of flaws to fail to maintain good character, even towards those who act with no friendship and do unpleasant things.
ai.modern: தன்னிடம் நட்பு கொள்ளாமல் இனிமையற்ற செயல்களைச் செய்பவரிடத்திலும், தான் பண்புடையவனாக நடந்து கொள்ளாமல் இருப்பது மிகத் தாழ்ந்த செயலாகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet defines the true test of good character (பண்பு). It states that even when facing people who show no friendship and commit unpleasant acts, one must not abandon one's own courteous nature. Failing to maintain good character towards such hostile people is considered the lowest form of behavior (கடை). True courtesy remains steadfast regardless of how others behave.

ai.literal: Rejoicing capable not-to-those great vast world daytime-even part having-fallen-it-is darkness.
ai.translation: For those who are unable to rejoice with others, this great vast world is plunged in darkness even during the day.
ai.modern: மற்றவர்களோடு சேர்ந்து மகிழ முடியாதவர்களுக்கு, இந்தப் பெரிய உலகமானது பகல் நேரத்திலும் இருளில்தான் இருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the isolated state of those who lack the good character to mingle and rejoice with others. The phrase 'nakal vallar allārkku' refers to people who cannot smile or share joy. For such people, the 'mā iru ñālam' (great vast world) offers no light. Even in the bright daytime, their world is 'pāl paṭṭaṉṟu iruḷ'—it has fallen into the nature of darkness, reflecting their inner gloom and social isolation.

ai.literal: character / he who is without / obtained / great wealth / good milk / vessel / by the impurity / having spoiled / like that
ai.translation: The great wealth obtained by a man without good character is like pure milk that has spoiled due to the impurity of its vessel.
ai.modern: நல்ல பண்பு இல்லாதவன் அடைந்த பெரிய செல்வமானது, பாத்திரத்தின் அழுக்கினால் அதில் ஊற்றி வைக்கப்பட்ட நல்ல பால் கெட்டுப்போவதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares a person lacking good character to an unclean vessel. Just as pure, good milk turns sour and becomes useless when poured into a dirty pot, great wealth becomes spoiled and useless when it is held by a person without noble qualities. The word 'கலம்' (vessel) represents the person's character, while 'நன்பால்' (good milk) represents the wealth they acquire.
